data.title: Run a bounded bug fix in an existing cloud environment
data.summary: Investigate a repository issue, produce a minimal patch and review test evidence before merging.

facts.text: Codex Cloud runs coding tasks in separate workspaces using a selected environment. Existing environments can be reused, and changes are reviewed before committing or opening a pull request.

prerequisites: Access to Codex Cloud; check account, client and workspace availability.
Authorized repository/ref, configured tools and setup requirements.
steps: Select the existing environment and confirm repository, branch/ref and issue scope.
Ask for reproduction and a reuse search before edits. Inspect environment setup and missing access.
Make the smallest fix and run a test that fails before the change and passes after it.
Inspect changed files, dependency changes and all reported checks. Keep any untested behavior explicit.
Open or update the appropriate pull request when authorized; review the diff and CI before merging.
data.output: a minimal patch, reproduction and before/after test receipt
validation: Report the blocked integration separately from local tests.
Find a real reproduction; do not present a non-regression test as evidence.
limitations: Sintra-authored procedure based on provider documentation or demonstrations; no execution in the named app was performed.
Availability and results depend on your inputs, enabled tools and permissions; a suggested practice result is not a measured outcome.
data.prompt: Use [existing cloud environment] for [repository/ref] to investigate [issue and reproduction]. Read project instructions and find an existing equivalent before editing. Reproduce the failure, propose a minimal fix and run a case that fails before and passes after. Inspect relevant callers and existing checks. Return the diff, exact test results, environment blockers and remaining risks. Reuse the appropriate pull request if one exists; keep merge and deployment within the project’s authorized release process.
tips: Task isolation does not prove the selected repository/ref is correct.
Keep test evidence tied to the patch commit.
